points.t: A pearly, shiny papule with rolled edge and fine vessels, or a sore that bleeds, crusts and never fully heals, on sun-exposed skin.
UV damage to basal keratinocytes switches on the Hedgehog pathway (PTCH1); latency 20–50 years; Gorlin syndrome is inherited PTCH1 loss.

Routine referral (NG12), suspected cancer pathway only if delay would matter because of site or size; specialist surgery first-line for most BCCs including nodular (BAD 2021); imiquimod or PDT for superficial BCC.
Periocular and nasal BCCs that invade deeply; morphoeic BCC with ill-defined edges; trigeminal trophic syndrome mimicking BCC.

points: **Intermittent intense and cumulative UV**, with a latency of decades (course teaching gave 20–50 years). Fair skin (Fitzpatrick I–II), age, male sex.

Other risks: previous BCC (about 40% get another within 3 years), radiotherapy, arsenic, immunosuppression (transplant), and **hydrochlorothiazide** (MHRA 2018: dose-dependent increased NMSC risk, mainly SCC).
**Hedgehog pathway:** most BCCs have loss of **PTCH1** or activating **SMO** mutations, which is why hedgehog inhibitors (vismodegib, sonidegib) work in advanced disease.
Histology: nests of basaloid cells with **peripheral palisading**, **retraction artefact** (clefting) and mucinous stroma.

items.name: Nodular (commonest)
items.t: Pearly/translucent papule-nodule, rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer ("rodent ulcer")

items.name: Superficial
items.t: Pink, scaly, thin plaque with a "thread-like" pearly edge; trunk and limbs; younger patients

items.name: Morphoeic / infiltrative
items.t: Ill-defined, scar-like, waxy, indurated plaque; subclinical spread; high-risk

items.name: Pigmented
items.t: Brown-blue-grey; commoner in skin of colour; melanoma DDx

items.name: Basosquamous
items.t: Mixed features; behaves more like SCC (metastatic potential)

points: Clinical + **dermoscopy:** **arborising (tree-like) vessels in sharp focus**; blue-grey ovoid nests/globules; spoke-wheel and leaf-like structures; ulceration; shiny white structures.
The skin cancer team confirms with **punch or excision biopsy**. Histology determines the subtype and risk.

items.t: BCC near the eye, nose or ear, large, rapidly growing or recurrent: consider the **suspected cancer pathway** because delay could matter (NG12 1.7.6).
Do not freeze, curette or apply imiquimod to an **undiagnosed** pigmented or nodular lesion: refer for diagnosis first.
Multiple BCCs in a young person, palmar pits or jaw cysts: think **Gorlin syndrome** and refer.

pearls.t: Imiquimod counselling: apply at bedtime, wash off after about 8 h; expect redness, crusting and erosion (it means the drug is working); stop and seek advice if there is severe reaction or flu-like illness.
Sun protection: SPF 30+ with high UVA rating, shade, hats (NICE NG34). Advise a self-check every month.
Hedgehog inhibitors: pregnancy prevention for women (and condoms for men on vismodegib); cramps, taste loss and weight loss are common.
